questions.q: Why run `sudo sshd -T | grep -i permitrootlogin` as a verification step, rather than just trusting that you edited the config file correctly?
options: sshd -T has no real purpose here
It shows the setting sshd is actually applying at runtime, confirming the edit took effect rather than assuming it did
It edits the config file directly
It only works before the service has been restarted
questions.explain: sshd -T prints the effective configuration sshd is currently using, which is the real test of whether an edit actually took effect — not just that it was typed into the file.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what makes a resume bullet about this project stronger?
options: Using broad phrases like 'improved security' without naming any tools
Naming the specific tools used (ufw, systemd, cron, SSH keys) and being honest that it was a lab project
Omitting any mention of verification or testing
Claiming it was production infrastructure for a real company
questions.explain: The lesson recommends naming concrete tools (which a hiring manager can quickly recognize) and being truthful about scope — a self-directed lab project, not production work for a real employer.

questions.q: In the Situation / What You Did / Result interview structure, what belongs in 'Result'?
options: A restatement of the situation
Something you can prove, like having verified each hardening step afterward via sshd -T, ufw status, and the logs
A list of every command typed, without context
A guess about what the interviewer wants to hear
questions.explain: The lesson frames 'Result' as the provable outcome — specifically, verification that each configured piece actually worked, not just that steps were followed.

questions.q: What does the lesson say separates someone who 'followed a checklist' from someone who 'understands a Linux server' in an interview setting?
options: Memorizing every command by heart
Being able to explain why a specific step had to happen in a particular order, such as allowing SSH before enabling the firewall
Typing commands quickly without looking at documentation
Having root access to more servers
questions.explain: The lesson specifically calls out being ready to explain the reasoning behind the ordering (e.g., allow SSH before enabling ufw) as the mark of real understanding, not just rote execution.

questions.q: What is recommended for a GitHub README documenting this capstone project?
options: Just a list of filenames with no explanation
A clear description of what the setup does, plus the actual systemd unit file and scripts kept in the repo alongside it
Only screenshots of the terminal, no text
A single sentence with no further detail
questions.explain: The lesson recommends a README that explains what the project does and lists its files, with the real .service file and scripts included in the repo so claims are backed by working files.
